about: Facts with one source only (certainty 'reference'). Send a second, independent source for each: a different catalogue, price guide or page, never the same one again. Values: a dated price page and the grade you assumed from the photo; stories: check every sentence and say agree or what is wrong.

items.story: A 1969 1-franc coin from Switzerland. The front shows Helvetia standing. The back shows the value in a wreath. Antoine Bovy engraved it, using front-side art by Albert Walch and back-side art by Friedrich Fisch. It is made of copper-nickel.

A 1963 5-rappen coin from Switzerland. The front shows Libertas looking to the right. The back shows a 5 in a wreath made of grapevines. Karl Schwenzer designed the front, and Carl Friedrich Voigt designed the back. It is made of copper-nickel.

A 2000 Dutch 5-euro-cent coin. The Dutch side shows a portrait of Queen Beatrix with the words BEATRIX KONINGIN DER NEDERLANDEN (Beatrix, Queen of the Netherlands). The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in copper-plated steel.

A 1986 French 20-centime coin. The front shows Marianne, the symbol of France, facing left, by Henri Lagriffoul; the back shows the value with olive and wheat stalks and the motto LIBERTÉ, ÉGALITÉ, FRATERNITÉ, by Adrien Dieudonné. Struck in aluminium-bronze.

A 1963 French 10-centime coin. The front shows Marianne, the symbol of France, facing left, by Henri Lagriffoul; the back shows the value with olive and wheat stalks and the motto LIBERTÉ, ÉGALITÉ, FRATERNITÉ, by Adrien Dieudonné. Struck in aluminium-bronze.
A 1968 half-franc coin from Switzerland. The front shows Helvetia standing. The back shows the value in a wreath. Antoine Bovy engraved it from a design by Albert Walch. It is made of copper-nickel.

A 1987 5-Deutsche-Mark coin from Germany. The front shows the German federal eagle. The back shows the value and the words DEUTSCHE MARK. This is the regular everyday coin made of Magnimat metal, not the silver one made for collectors. Magnimat is a nickel-based coin metal.

A 1962 1-franc coin from France. The front shows La Semeuse (the Sower) walking to the left with the words REPUBLIQUE FRANCAISE, designed by Oscar Roty. The back shows 1 FRANC, an olive branch, the motto LIBERTE, EGALITE, FRATERNITE, and the date 1962. It is made of nickel.

A 1971 2 new pence from United Kingdom. The obverse shows Arnold Machin Elizabeth II; the reverse shows Plume of ostrich feathers in coronet; NEW PENCE (Ironside). Struck in bronze (97 Cu / 2.5 Zn / 0.5 Sn).
A 1971 half-franc coin from Switzerland. The front shows Helvetia standing. The back shows the value in a wreath. Antoine Bovy engraved it from a design by Albert Walch. It is made of copper-nickel.

A 1999 1-franc coin from France. The front shows La Semeuse (the Sower) walking to the left with the words REPUBLIQUE FRANCAISE, designed by Oscar Roty. The back shows 1 FRANC, an olive branch, the motto LIBERTE, EGALITE, FRATERNITE, and the date 1999. It is made of nickel.

items.story: A 1918 20-heller coin from Austria, struck in iron during the First World War under Emperor Charles I, when copper and nickel went to the war. The side shown has a large 20 in an oak wreath with the date 1918 below and no lettering; the other side shows the crowned double-headed eagle with the Austrian shield. Stefan Schwartz engraved it.

A 1977 2 new pence from United Kingdom. The obverse shows Arnold Machin Elizabeth II; the reverse shows Plume of ostrich feathers in coronet; NEW PENCE (Ironside). Struck in bronze (97 Cu / 2.5 Zn / 0.5 Sn).

A 1965 1-franc coin from France. The front shows La Semeuse (the Sower) walking to the left with the words REPUBLIQUE FRANCAISE, designed by Oscar Roty. The back shows 1 FRANC, an olive branch, the motto LIBERTE, EGALITE, FRATERNITE, and the date 1965. It is made of nickel.

A 2002 German 50-euro-cent coin. Germany's side shows the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin, designed by Reinhart Heinsdorff, ringed by the 12 European stars. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.

A 2002 Italian 20-euro-cent coin. Italy's side shows Umberto Boccioni's sculpture Unique Forms of Continuity in Space, adapted by Maria Angela Cassol. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.

A 2013 Maltese 5-euro-cent coin. Malta's side shows the altar stone of the prehistoric Mnajdra temple, with the word MALTA. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in copper-plated steel.

A 1967 Hungarian 1-forint coin. The front shows the arms of the People's Republic of Hungary, with wheat and a star; the back shows a large 1 FORINT and the Budapest mint mark BP. Struck in aluminium.

A 1969 French half franc. The front shows the Sower — a woman scattering seeds at sunrise, one of France's most loved coin designs, designed by Oscar Roty in 1900. The back carries France's motto: liberty, equality, brotherhood.

A 1971 German 50 pfennig. The front shows a woman planting a young oak tree. She honors the 'rubble women' who cleared and rebuilt Germany's bombed cities after the war — planting new life where destruction had been.

A 2007 Italian 10-euro-cent coin. Italy's side shows a detail of Botticelli's painting The Birth of Venus, adapted by Claudia Momoni. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.

A 2002 German 10-euro-cent coin. Germany's side shows the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin, designed by Reinhart Heinsdorff, ringed by the 12 European stars. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.

A 2009 Slovak 2-euro-cent coin. Slovakia's side shows Kriváň, a famous peak in the Tatra mountains, with the Slovak double cross and the word SLOVENSKO, designed by Drahomír Zobek. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in copper-plated steel.

A 2010 Italian 2-euro-cent coin. Italy's side shows the Mole Antonelliana tower in Turin, designed by Luciana De Simoni. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in copper-plated steel.

A 2001 Dutch 20-euro-cent coin. The Dutch side shows a portrait of Queen Beatrix with the words BEATRIX KONINGIN DER NEDERLANDEN (Beatrix, Queen of the Netherlands). The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.

A 1974 French 20-centime coin. The front shows Marianne, the symbol of France, facing left, by Henri Lagriffoul; the back shows the value with olive and wheat stalks and the motto LIBERTÉ, ÉGALITÉ, FRATERNITÉ, by Adrien Dieudonné. Struck in aluminium-bronze.

A 2008 Maltese 10-euro-cent coin. Malta's side shows the national coat of arms (a shield of the Maltese flag under a crown, with olive and palm branches) and the word MALTA. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.
A 2014 Dutch 5 euro cent. It shows King Willem-Alexander, who had taken the throne just a year earlier in 2013. The twelve stars around him stand for the European Union.

A 2010 German 2-euro-cent coin. Germany's side shows an oak twig, designed by Rolf Lederbogen, ringed by the 12 European stars. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in copper-plated steel.
A 2006 5 centavos from Brazil. The obverse shows Tiradentes portrait, BRASIL, dove and Inconfidência triangle; the reverse shows Southern Cross globe, 5 CENTAVOS, 2006. Struck in copper-plated steel.

A 2011 German 20-euro-cent coin. Germany's side shows the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin, designed by Reinhart Heinsdorff, ringed by the 12 European stars. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.

A 2002 Italian 50-euro-cent coin, from the first year of the euro. Italy's side shows the statue of Emperor Marcus Aurelius on horseback on the patterned pavement of the Campidoglio square in Rome. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.

A 2002 Portuguese 20-euro-cent coin, from the first year of the euro. Portugal's side shows the royal seal of 1142, with seven castles and five shields, designed by Vítor Santos. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.
A 1985 German 50 pfennig with the same planting-woman design. The little oak sapling she tends was meant to grow strong like the new Germany — the design stayed on this coin for over fifty years.

A 1960 French 1 franc. The Sower walks through a field at sunrise scattering seed — a design France loved so much it stayed on coins for more than sixty years. The olive branch and the words liberty, equality, brotherhood are on the back.
A 1971 French half franc. The Sower strides across the front at dawn, a symbol of France planting its future. These small coins were everyday money across France for years.

A 2002 Italian 20-euro-cent coin. Italy's side shows Umberto Boccioni's sculpture Unique Forms of Continuity in Space, adapted by Maria Angela Cassol. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in Nordic gold, a golden copper alloy.

A 2008 Maltese 1-euro coin. Malta's side shows the eight-pointed Maltese Cross, designed by Noel Galea Bason. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. It is made of two metals: a copper-nickel center inside a nickel-brass ring.

A 2014 Swiss 5-franc coin. The front shows the head of an alpine herdsman; the back shows the Swiss cross shield and 5 FR. inside an alpine wreath. Designed by Paul Burkhard and struck in copper-nickel (75% copper, 25% nickel).

The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. It is made of two metals: a nickel-brass center inside a copper-nickel ring.

A 2003 German 2-euro coin. Germany's side shows the federal eagle, designed by Heinz Hoyer and Sneschana Russewa-Hoyer. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. It is made of two metals: a nickel-brass center inside a copper-nickel ring.

A 1976 American quarter made for the country's 200th birthday. George Washington is on the front as always, but the back is special: a Revolutionary War drummer boy, made only for the Bicentennial. The double date 1776-1976 marks two hundred years of independence.

A 1989 Swiss 20 rappen. Libertas gazes to the right on the front — the same liberty goddess Switzerland has put on its coins for over a century. The big 20 in a wreath on the back leaves no doubt what it's worth.

A 1976 1 yen coin from Japan. One side shows a young tree, with the words 日本国 and 一円. The other side shows a big 1 and the date in Showa regnal years (Showa 51 = 1976). Struck in aluminum.

A 1987 5 pesos coin from Mexico. The value side shows a $ sign, a big 5, the year 1987 and the Mo mint mark, with a scroll ornament and a beaded rim. The obverse shows the national arms. Struck in brass.

A 2000 100 won coin from South Korea. The value side shows the year 2000, a big 100 and the words 한국은행 (Bank of Korea), with a beaded rim. The obverse shows a portrait of Yi Sun-sin. Struck in copper-nickel.

A 1987 500 lire coin from Italy. The obverse shows the head of Italia, the female symbol of Italy. The reverse shows the Palazzo del Quirinale with the Dioscuri statues, the value L. 500, the number 500 in Braille on the ring, wheat ears, the date and the mint mark R. Struck as a bimetallic coin, with a bronzital (aluminium-bronze) centre and an acmonital (stainless steel) ring.
A 1971 1 penny from United Kingdom. The obverse shows Arnold Machin Elizabeth II; the reverse shows crowned portcullis; NEW PENNY (Ironside). Struck in bronze (97 Cu / 2.5 Zn / 0.5 Sn).
A 1998 1 penny from United Kingdom. The obverse shows Ian Rank-Broadley Elizabeth II; the reverse shows crowned portcullis; ONE PENNY (Ironside). Struck in copper-plated steel.
A 2010 1 penny from United Kingdom. The obverse shows Ian Rank-Broadley Elizabeth II; the reverse shows Royal Shield segment; ONE PENNY (Matthew Dent). Struck in copper-plated steel.

A 1982 10 yen coin from Japan. One side shows the Phoenix Hall of the Byodoin temple, with the words 日本国 and 十円. The other side shows a large 10 inside a wreath of bay laurel (tokiwa), and the date in Showa regnal years (Showa 57 = 1982). Struck in bronze (95% copper, 3-4% zinc, 1-2% tin).
A 1986 0.5 franc from France. The obverse shows La Semeuse left (Oscar Roty); the reverse shows 1/2 FRANC; olive sprig, LIBERTE, EGALITE, FRATERNITE, date. Struck in nickel.
A 1965 1 yen coin from Japan. One side shows a young tree, with the words 日本国 and 一円. The other side shows a big 1 and the date in Showa regnal years (Showa 40 = 1965). Struck in aluminum.
A 1967 Dutch 1-gulden coin. The front shows Queen Juliana; the back shows the crowned Dutch coat of arms with a lion. Struck in silver (72% fine).

A 2015 10 dollar coin from Jamaica. It shows the national arms, with a crocodile crest, Taino supporters and a motto ribbon, and the words JAMAICA and TEN DOLLARS with the year 2015. The coin is round. Struck in nickel-clad steel.

A AH 1378 (1958) 1 qirsh from Saudi Arabia. Value side قرش واحد, big ١, Hijri ١٣٧٨ (AH 1378 ≈ 1958–59 CE); المملكة العربية السعودية is in the legend around the arms on the other side. Struck in cupronickel.

A 2003 1000 đồng coin from Vietnam. The emblem side shows a star and a cog inside a wreath of rice, with the words CỘNG HÒA XÃ HỘI CHỦ NGHĨA VIỆT NAM and the year 2003. The reverse shows the value, 1000 ĐỒNG. Struck in brass-plated steel.

items.story: A 1968 10 new pence coin from the United Kingdom. The obverse shows Arnold Machin's portrait of Elizabeth II. The reverse shows a crowned lion walking with its head turned to the front, with the words NEW PENCE; the design is by Christopher Ironside. Struck in copper-nickel (75% copper, 25% nickel).

A 1934 10 centavos coin from Guatemala. One side shows the coat of arms - a quetzal, crossed rifles and swords, and laurel - with the words REPUBLICA DE GUATEMALA, the fineness 0.720 and the year 1934. The other side shows a quetzal perched on a column, with the words LEY DE 26 DE NOVIEMBRE DE 1924, 10 and CENTAVOS. Struck in silver, .720 fine.

A 2010 2 pesos coin from Mexico. The value side shows a $ sign, a large 2, the year 2010 and the Mo mint mark, with the glyphs of the Ring of Days from the Aztec Sun Stone around the outer ring. The obverse shows the national arms. Struck as a bimetallic coin, with an aluminum-bronze centre and a stainless steel outer ring.
A 1997 1 penny from United Kingdom. The obverse shows Raphael Maklouf Elizabeth II; the reverse shows crowned portcullis; ONE PENNY (Ironside). Struck in copper-plated steel.

A 1883 10 rappen coin from Switzerland. The obverse shows the head of Libertas facing right. The reverse shows the number 10 inside a wreath. The designers were Karl Schwenzer and Carl Friedrich Voigt. Struck in copper-nickel (75% copper, 25% nickel).

A 1946 French 5-franc coin, struck just after the Second World War. The front shows Marianne, the symbol of France, wearing a laurel wreath, by André Lavrillier; the back shows 5 FRANCS inside a laurel wreath with the letters RF (République Française). Struck in aluminium.

A 1966 1 won coin from South Korea. One side shows a Rose of Sharon flower (Hibiscus syriacus), with the words 일원 and 한국은행. The other side shows the words THE BANK OF KOREA, a big 1 and the year 1966. Struck in brass.
A 1966 20 cents from Australia. The obverse shows Elizabeth II; the reverse shows Stuart Devlin platypus in water; big 20. Struck in cupronickel.

A 1962 20 centavos coin from Cuba. The reverse shows a portrait of José Martí with the date. The arms side shows the words REPUBLICA DE CUBA and the national shield (the Escudo - a key, stripes and a palm), with oak and laurel branches and a star on a Phrygian cap, and the words VEINTE CENTAVOS. Struck in copper-nickel.

A 1993 10-cent coin from Jamaica. One side shows the coat of arms of Jamaica. A crocodile sits on top. Two Taino people hold the shield. The shield has a cross with pineapples on it. The coin also says JAMAICA, TEN CENTS, and 1993. It also says the motto OUT OF MANY, ONE PEOPLE. The coin is made of steel with a thin coat of nickel on it.
A 1951 10 lire from Vatican City. The obverse shows Pius XII portrait; the reverse shows standing Prudentia; CITTA' DEL VATICANO, 1951, L. 10, PRVDENTIA. Struck in aluminum.

A 1959 20-rappen coin from Switzerland. The front shows Libertas facing right, designed by Karl Schwenzer. The back shows the number 20 inside a wreath, designed by Carl Friedrich Voigt. It is made of copper-nickel (75% copper and 25% nickel).

A 1967 20-centavo coin from Mexico. The front shows the coat of arms of Mexico. The back shows the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan. Two volcanoes stand behind it. Their names are Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl. A liberty cap shines above the pyramid. The back also has a big 20, the word CENTAVOS, the date 1967, and the Mo mint mark. The coin is made of brass. The brass is 95% copper and 5% zinc.

items.story: A 1950 Mexican 25-centavo coin. The back shows a balance scale and a scroll marked LEY (law) under a cap of liberty with rays of light; the front carries the national arms. Struck in silver (30% fine).
A 1973 10-cent coin from Singapore. One side shows a crowned seahorse. The value side shows two stalks of rice, a large 10, and the words CENTS, 1973, and SINGAPORE. It is made of copper-nickel.

A 2012 South Korean 10-won coin. One side shows the Dabotap Pagoda, an eighth-century stone pagoda; the other shows a large 10 and the name of the Bank of Korea in Korean. Struck in copper-clad aluminium.

A 2013 South Korean 10-won coin. One side shows the Dabotap Pagoda, an eighth-century stone pagoda; the other shows a large 10 and the name of the Bank of Korea in Korean. Struck in copper-clad aluminium.

An Austrian 2 groschen from 1925. One side is the federal cross with the date, the other a large 2 over the word GROSCHEN. 1925 is the year Austria introduced the schilling, and the groschen was its small change.

A German 1 euro cent from 2005: the oak twig that Germany kept from its old pfennig coins, ringed by the twelve EU stars. Germany's euro coins carry a mint letter, and this one is J, struck in Hamburg.

A 1997 1-piso coin from the Philippines. The side in the photo shows José Rizal. He is a national hero of the Philippines. The coin says Republika ng Pilipinas. That means Republic of the Philippines in English. It also has a big 1, the word PISO, and the date 1997.

A 1989 five-hundred-peso coin from Mexico with Francisco I. Madero, who started the Mexican Revolution in 1910, and a large $500 below him. Inflation made coins this big in the 1980s; in 1993 Mexico dropped three zeros from its money. There is no photo of this coin yet.
A 1958 Vatican 20 lire showing Charity (Caritas) standing with children. It was struck in Rome for Pope Pius XII as a standard circulation issue with a mintage of 60,000.

A 1991 Swedish 1 krona with the stylized portrait of Carl XVI Gustaf. This copper-nickel design, used from 1982 to 2000, was succeeded by a new portrait in 2001 before the smaller modern coin arrived in 2016.
A 1970 Portuguese 20 centavos with the five escutcheons (quinas) of the Portuguese shield forming a cross.
A 1994 Mexican 10 centavos - the small stainless-steel coin with the Ring of the Sacrifice from the Aztec calendar stone on this side.
A 1974 Bahamian cent - the first year the newly independent Bahamas put its own coat of arms on the cent. A starfish is on the other side.

items.story: A Sandy the Pony ride token from Meijer stores in the USA, with no date. It reads FREE PONY RIDE on one side and MEIJER IS FOR KIDS on the other, good for one free pony ride. It is made of brass.
